question: Should `scripts/pr` permanently reject all non-main prepare and merge commands in favor of the separate reviewed release-branch flow?
rationale: The fail-closed guard prevents the observed accidental rebase onto `origin/main`, but it also intentionally removes an operator path; only release ownership can confirm that compatibility tradeoff.

options.title: Keep the main-only guard
options.body: Confirm the reviewed release-branch landing flow as the sole supported non-main path and keep the pre-mutation rejection and tests.

options.title: Make commands base-aware
options.body: Refactor prepare and merge orchestration to use the PR base safely, with focused release-branch proof before landing.

recommendation.title: Keep the main-only guard
recommendation.body: Confirm the reviewed release-branch landing flow as the sole supported non-main path and keep the pre-mutation rejection and tests.

likelyOwner.reason: This contributor supplied the live release-branch failure probe and has recent release-test activity, making them the strongest available operator-contract owner.
